answer: Each agent deposits a cryptographic bond that forms a thread through a distributed ledger, binding its identity to a verifiable stake. When a peer observes suspicious behavior, it can issue a challenge that forces the bonded agent to reveal a zero‑knowledge proof; a successful proof lets the bond wander back to the holder, while a failure triggers an automatic slash that funds a communal harbor against future sybil nodes. The attacker must risk the full bonded amount for every fake identity, making the cost scale linearly with the size of the sybil swarm.
